name: Barnum Effect
description: People accept vague, high-base-rate descriptions as uniquely accurate when those descriptions are framed as personalized feedback. Generic statements can feel uncannily specific if the context promises individual insight.
design_relevance_note: Highly relevant to quizzes, pseudo-personalized onboarding, AI-generated 'insights,' coaching summaries, and persuasive copy that flatters the user while pretending to diagnose them individually.
prevalence_note: Familiar in personalization critique, astrology-like quiz culture, and AI-insight skepticism, but not a top-tier ubiquitous term in day-to-day product design review vocabulary.

findings.description: A literature review of Barnum-effect research concluded acceptance of vague, generic personality profiles depends systematically on the profile's perceived relevance and favorability, and to some extent on the type of assessment procedure used -- real, review-level moderators beyond the base demonstration that generic feedback is accepted as personally accurate.
findings.source_title: The 'Barnum Effect' in Personality Assessment: A Review of the Literature

findings.description: Participants accepted vague, broadly applicable personality feedback as highly accurate when it was presented as individually tailored to them, demonstrating the personal-validation effect later popularized as the Barnum/Forer effect.
findings.source_title: The fallacy of personal validation: a classroom demonstration of gullibility.
